HG14-fxw1:
Let the child speak without handing over the steering wheel

It’s possible to let the ‘younger’ parts of you express themselves without surrendering your adult judgement to an outside caretaker, and without literally reverting to a younger age. Instead, the aim is to access the positive aspects of ‘younger’ feeling states, such as a sense of wonder or playfulness, more direct sensory experiences, vulnerability, need, and a desire to carry fewer decisions.
HG14-fxw2:
Love doesn’t have to wait for trust

Even if your inner child does not believe that you love him or her, you can still love him or her. Trust can question your promises, remember when you failed to protect him or her, and take its time.

You can say, out loud or in your head, “Okay. I believe that you don’t believe me, but I still love you. You don’t have to love me back. Please tell me what is not okay with you.”

Respond to complaints, which are likely to include something true. Showing that you love him or her can include some or all of the following: listening to him or her when he or she is angry without hitting back, owning up to what was not okay, working on being less likely to turn on him or her, and other ways of making it up to him or her. Other ways of showing that you love him or her include taking care of him or her by buying and cooking food, setting limits, taking him or her to doctor’s appointments, and doing what you say you will do. Just not hitting back is not enough; you also need to love your inner child.

Be aware of what you are teaching your other positions. You might be teaching your inner child that you are going to love him or her no matter what, but you might also be teaching him or her that he or she is responsible for believing your love, and that if he or she does not, it is his or her fault. The position that is making the vow to love the inner child no matter what, and the position that is blaming the inner child for not taking in the love, might be separate positions, or they might be one position, or you might be blending them. It might not be based on chronological age.

When you're placing your younger self on trial, how valuable is it for you to consider how valuable it might have been for your younger self at the time to be doing what they did, given what they knew at the time? How valuable is it for you to consider what options were available to them at the time, and how tolerable they were? How valuable is it for you to consider the consequences of their actions at the time? How valuable is it for you to consider that whilst their actions might have caused harm to you and others, punishing yourself now will not give them the capacity they needed at the time, and that it is more useful to work on what you can do now to deal with the harm that was caused?

WORKING WITH YOUR INNER CHILD:
HG14-fxw3:
The Nurturer

THE NURTURER: As a Nurturer one of the most important things that you can do is to enjoy your inner child, to sit back and not feel like you have to move their feelings and to say to them that you are really glad that they are here in this moment. Children need to be enjoyed.

It’s okay that you’re feeling the way you are feeling.

I want you to know I’m here for you.

You don’t need to do anything right now.

It’s okay that you’re not too much. You can be small here.

You can be angry here.

You can be sad here.

The Protector

I’m going to be here for you.

The Protector:

Work with your Protector to set boundaries together. They might be small, like “I’m going to leave this conversation because it’s not safe,” or “I’m going to stop texting someone who destabilizes me.” They might be self-care related, like “I’m going to eat” or “I’m going to get sleep.” They might be trust-related, like “I’m going to keep this promise to myself” or “I’m not going to leave you alone to deal with these adult things.”

A lot of inner child work fails because we do all the fluffy stuff, but then we go text the person who destabilizes us or don’t eat or don’t do whatever thing we were meant to be doing. Trust comes from being able to handle adult things.

If you can’t bring up the warmth stuff yet, that’s okay, you can always do something to be protective of your inner child. Make sure they’re small enough that you can do them. If you can’t, figure out what’s getting in the way of doing them. Are you scared? Tired? Don’t know how? Is there a practical obstacle in your way? Did you set yourself up to do it successfully? Be careful not to define doing the thing successfully as “feeling good about it” or “being able to check it off a list.”
HG33-fxw1:
Appendix D: Anxiety — body first

Remember that often the anxiety comes from a protector part, a part of yourself who is trying to help you, but who believes you are in danger, or may be shamed, or abandoned, or fail, or be exposed, or become sick, or rejected, or lose control, or suffer something else unbearable. Therefore, instead of an interrogation, start with yourself:

Always work with yourself by first taking care of your body, then your inner child, then some inner inquiry, and then some action:

Inner child love

Inner child love: Put a hand over your heart, and a hand on your solar plexis, and say lovingly, “Little one, you are not alone. You don’t have to fix this. I’m here now. The adult is listening.” Don’t just say the words, but say them in a way that you are talking to the inner child, who is frightened.

Reduced breathing / Buteyko-style breathing

Reduce your breathing. (NOTE: there are some good things to be said for slowing down the breathing, for some who overbreathe or are panicked, and this part is based on the Buteyko approach. But please don’t force yourself to hold your breath and suffer air hunger, which can make you more anxious for a short period. Proceed slowly.) Take small inhales through the nose, and quiet exhales, with pauses only if comfortable. Can you quiet your breathing? STOP if you feel dizzy, strained, or panicky, or experience any other medical concerns.
HG33-fxw2:
Anxiety script

Where am my body? What are my feet doing? How am I sitting in the chair? How am I breathing? How is my body in the room?

Little one, if you can hear me, I want you to know that I am here. Protector, thank you for alerting me. You don’t have to scream. I got your message.

Now if there is something we need to do, show me what the first thing is that we should do, right now. And if there is nothing we need to do, help my body stand down, and know that I am not going to abandon you, but I am also not going to worship you. I am going to listen to you, reality test what you are saying, and then take some action.
